youtube.title: UNDER THE HOOD
youtube.summary: Graham Hood reflects on a 50-year aviation career and the unexpected lessons life has taught him, using the story of an airport firefighter’s final emergency call-out to explore preparation, mistakes, integrity and regret. He looks back on leaving aviation over vaccine mandates, acknowledges what he sacrificed, but remains convinced he made the right choice. As he prepares for his New Zealand tour, Graham encourages us to stop rushing towards the next goal and instead embrace the journey, where character is built and life unfolds. Don't miss Hoody on a Roadie Discover more from Hoody at Club Grubbery or find him on Facebook and X

youtube.title: The food pyramid as it existed came out of the US Department of Agriculture, not health actually...
youtube.summary: "The food pyramid as it existed came out of the US Department of Agriculture, not health actually, in the 1970s, which was a medical misadventure and probably now just a scam, should've been abandoned years ago." - Prof Grant Schofield, Professor of Public Health at Auckland University of Technology If decades of official food advice got the basics wrong, how much damage could that have done to public health? 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/prof-grant-schofield-professor-of-public-health-at-auckland-university-of-technology-how-to-fix-a-broken-health-system #RCRMedia

youtube.title: Maybe parents just need to start parenting a bit more.
youtube.summary: "Maybe parents just need to start parenting a bit more." - Nicole McKee, ACT Deputy Leader If parents can take the phone away, set the rules and say no, why should taxpayers fund a massive government system to do the parenting for them? 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/nicole-mckee-act-deputy-leader-act-promises-to-wind-up-waitangi-tribunal #RCRMedia

youtube.title: If we fined Twitter something like 10% of their annual revenue, for a country of 5 million people...
youtube.summary: "If we fined Twitter something like 10% of their annual revenue, for a country of 5 million people, what is the interest in Twitter to have that liability? It's zero. They're like: 'We can just drop these 5 million people like that.'" - Joshua Riley, Sovereign Leader If the potential fines dwarf the value of the NZ market, why would X or Facebook take the risk? Could regulation designed to control Big Tech instead convince Big Tech to simply drop New Zealand? 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/a-political-agenda-with-maree-buscke-sandra-goudie-joshua-riley-are-nzs-laws-putting-rights-and-freedoms-at-risk #RCRMedia #APoliticalAgenda

youtube.title: 18 Votes From Flipping Mt Albert
youtube.summary: 18 Votes From Flipping Mt Albert "We could've actually turned it." - Melissa Lee, National List MP for Mt Albert Melissa Lee says just 18 votes separated her from winning a traditionally strong Labour electorate. How many supposedly "safe" seats could change if turnout shifted even slightly? Simon O'Connor and Melissa Lee discuss the importance of voting. 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/melissa-lee-national-list-mp-for-mt-albert-why-every-vote-matters #RCRMedia

youtube.title: HARETE HIPANGO-BROWNLIE
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke talks with Harete Hipango-Brownlie former National MP and now NZ First candidate for Whanganui, about why she left National over its handling of Covid-era protests and mandates. Harete discusses cost-of-living and housing pressures in her electorate, criticises Māori political leadership over child abuse cases and Māori funding accountability, and argues New Zealanders should hold politicians to account for decisions made during the pandemic. For more on Harete For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: THE FOURTH ESTATE
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke hosts barrister Matt Robson and filmmaker Gaylene Barnes to dissect Labour's vague new AI policy, a disputed media account of a candidate meeting confrontation over vaccine questions, and the censure of a Nelson GP for prescribing ivermectin during COVID. Robson and Barnes also clash gently over claims of left-wing media bias, with Barnes arguing independent creators face an “oxygen of amplification” blackout from legacy outlets. For more from the guests Matt Robson and at the NZ Fabian Society Gaylene Barnes , her film River of Freedom , the book Heart of the Protest and on Facebook , and her web-series The+Tribute Look beyond the headlines with RCR Bites , FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: MARK HOOPER
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan talks with Federated Farmers board member Mark Hooper about the rural policies from six parties debated ahead of the election. Hooper welcomes cross-party appetite for productivity growth but flags concerns over Labour's ETS settings, the Greens' regenerative farming push, and Te Pāti Māori's proposed governance structures, while backing calls from National and ACT for fewer rules and stronger property rights. For more from Federated Farmers visit their website or find them on Facebook and X

youtube.title: RIDING SHOTGUN
youtube.summary: Rachel Stewart examines the controversy surrounding New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s planned attendance at the 25th anniversary 9/11 commemorations, including criticism from victims’ families over his comments, political associations and appointment of Ramzi Kassem. She questions whether Mamdani’s presence is appropriate and argues that the families of those killed should have the final say. Discover more from Rachel on Substack and X
